extracted.intended_audience: qualitative health researchers, manuscript authors, peer reviewers, and journal editors
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive reporting guideline (CCQR) defining what to include when writing and reviewing qualitative research manuscripts in global health, organized into 14 reporting categories to improve transparency, rigor, and usability of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Draws and attracts the reader and entails precisely what the paper covers; must be of relevance to in-text content and precise. Include types of study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the methodology/type of study in the title where appropriate so readers immediately understand the research approach; make titles attractive yet precise and reflective of the study focus and design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Key elements of research including background, introduction, purpose, methodology, results, and conclusion. Under the abstract, include keywords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write an abstract that succinctly states the problem, objectives/research questions, design and methods, key results (major findings), and conclusions/implications. Include keywords for indexing. Consider writing the abstract last by pulling one representative sentence or phrase from each main section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim/objectives and purpose of the study. Relevance/justification of research question/connection to existing knowledge. Problem statement/rationale. Describing existing knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state the research problem, aims/objectives, research questions, and rationale. Explain how the study connects to and adds to existing literature and identify the target audience. Keep the introduction concise and aligned with methods and objectives so reviewers/readers can assess fit between question and approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Research design/theoretical framework/research paradigm. Rationale for chosen methodology. Study population (characteristics, sample size, inclusion, and exclusion criteria). Study site. Sampling technique. Researchers and participants relationship. Data collection technique/methods (e.g., in-depth interviews, focus group discussions (FGDs), observation, memos, field notes, audio recording, and video recording). Data collection process (period of data collection and timing of interview). Data collection tools (interview guide). Data analysis and data management (transcription, software, coding, theme generation, coding tree, number of data coders, data security, and data anonymity). Reflexivity. Reporting guidelines used in reporting the study. Transparency in all processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a full account of design and theoretical stance, and justify methodological choices. Report participant selection and recruitment (inclusion/exclusion, sample size rationale, sampling strategy), study setting, and researcher–participant relationships (including who conducted data collection). Describe data collection methods in detail (tools, pretesting, timing, duration, repeated interviews if any, and procedures for audio/video/notes). Describe data analysis steps: transcription procedures, coding approach, theme generation, coding tree, software used, number of coders, processes for intercoder reliability, triangulation, participant checking, and documentation of any methodological changes during the study. Report data management (security, anonymization). Include reflexivity statements about researcher characteristics and influence. State which reporting guideline/checklist was used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trustworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: How it is achieved? Which techniques were used? Credibility (e.g., prolonged engagement and member checking), transferability, dependability, conformability, and authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe specific strategies used to establish rigor (e.g., prolonged engagement, triangulation, member checking/participant feedback, thick description for transferability, audit trails for dependability and confirmability). Explicitly report how each trustworthiness criterion was addressed and provide examples or evidence (e.g., quotes, documentation of checks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical clearance and ethical approval: document to be available per request. Participant’s confidentiality and anonymity. Informed consent and procedure of taking informed consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report ethics committee approvals (with reference/ID where possible), processes for obtaining informed consent (written/verbal), measures to protect confidentiality and anonymity, data storage and access, and any particular ethical issues encountered (e.g., vulnerable populations, sensitive topics). State availability of documentation on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary and clear statement of findings. Research findings. Major and minor themes. Narration, quotes, and field notes. Diagrams, box, photographs, and video links (clear presentation of findings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a clear synthesis of findings organized by themes (distinguish major and minor themes). Use illustrative quotations, fieldnote excerpts, and visual displays (diagrams, tables, figures) to support interpretations. Ensure presentation is coherent and links back to research questions. Provide sufficient context for quotes (without breaching confidentiality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Any biases (selection bias, publication bias, and heterogeneity). Interpretation of study results. Summary of major findings and comparison with the existing literature and theory. Alternative explanation of findings. Implication, transferability, strength, and limitation of study contribution to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret findings in light of prior literature and theory, acknowledge possible biases and limitations, discuss alternative explanations, and outline implications for practice, policy, or further research. Address transferability/generalizability (how findings may apply to other contexts) and situate contribution to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Describing implications. Conclusion should come from analysis and interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure conclusions are grounded in the reported analysis and interpretation (not overstated). Highlight key implications, summarize contribution succinctly, and avoid introducing new data in the conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength and limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Strength and limitations. How valuable are the study results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly list study strengths and limitations, discussing the impact of limitations on findings and interpretations, and justify why results are valuable despite constraints. Be transparent about methodological trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation for further studies and to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide actionable, evidence-based recommendations for future research, policy, or practice, grounded in study findings. Distinguish between suggestions for research methods and substantive recommendations for the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Source of funding and other support received during the study process. Role of funders in data collection, interpretation, and reporting funding source (financial and nonfinancial support). Financial support for authorship or publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose all funding sources, grants, and in-kind support and describe the funders' role (if any) in study design, data collection, analysis, interpretation, writing, or publication. Declare any payments or waivers related to authorship or publication fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the information sources used/citations. Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete and accurate references to all cited literature and data sources. Include appendices or supplementary materials (e.g., interview guides, coding frameworks, search histories) to support transparency and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential influence on the study and how it was managed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare any potential conflicts of interest (financial, personal, professional) and describe measures taken to manage or mitigate their influence on study design, conduct, analysis, and reporting.
